title: Acids, Bases and pH (KS4 Chemistry)
subject: Chemistry
strapline: The pH scale, neutralisation and salt-making reactions.
facts: The pH scale runs from 0 to 14 and measures how acidic or alkaline a solution is.
pH below 7 is acidic, pH 7 is neutral, pH above 7 is alkaline.
Acids produce hydrogen ions (H⁺) in solution; alkalis produce hydroxide ions (OH⁻).
A base neutralises an acid; a soluble base is called an alkali.
Acid + metal → salt + hydrogen; acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide.
Universal indicator shows pH by colour: red (strong acid) through green (neutral) to purple (strong alkali).

quick_quiz.q: What ion do all acids produce in solution?
What are the products of acid + base?
What pH is a neutral solution?

teacher_tips: Anchor the pH scale with everyday substances (lemon, water, soap).
Drill the three general reaction patterns until they are automatic.
Test the gas: hydrogen (squeaky pop) vs CO₂ (limewater turns milky).
